'''Leti''', or '''Mangisa''', is a Bantu language of [[Cameroon]], spoken by the [[Mengisa people]].  Most Mengisa have switched to the [[Eton language]], though a number of them continue to use Leti as a secret [[Sacred language|ritual language]].  A smaller number speak Leti as their mother tongue.<ref name=e18/>

Leti is quite close to [[Ki language|Tuki]] and may be a dialect.<ref name=H>Hammarström (2015) Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: a comprehensive review: online appendices</ref> It is also closely related to [[Eton language|Eton]].<ref name="ALCAM2012"/>

Mengisa is spoken in the northern part of [[Sa'a, Cameroon|Sa'a]] commune (in [[Lekié]] department, Central Region).<ref name="ALCAM2012">{{cite book|editor-last=Binam Bikoi|editor-first=Charles|date=2012|title=Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM)|trans-title=Linguistic Atlas of Cameroon|volume=1: Inventaire des langues|language=fr|location=Yaoundé|publisher=CERDOTOLA|series=Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale (ALAC)|isbn=9789956796069}}</ref>
